version.changelog:
Initial release; renamed skill from aux-mcp to aux.

- Skill name changed from "aux-mcp" to "aux" throughout.
- Updated install path in documentation to use the new name.
- No changes to contract, features, or functionality.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed Spotify control skill, with normal Spotify account access risks but no artifact-backed deception or unrelated behavior found.

dimensions.detail: Spotify client credentials, OAuth login, local callback, and network use are proportionate for a Spotify MCP server and are described in the setup instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed through npm/npx and OpenClaw MCP registration; package metadata matched the stated spotify-aux package and repository, and no package lifecycle install script was found in package.json.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some triggers are broad, such as mood, weather/time, and “keep it going,” so users should expect the agent to interpret casual music-related prompts as Spotify actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses token storage under ~/.aux-mcp and local skill installation under ~/.openclaw; auto-DJ and party helpers can keep local session state or run continuing helper processes when invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s Spotify MCP purpose matches its capabilities: music search, playback, queueing, playlist/taste analysis, party rooms, and auto-DJ behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving an MCP server Spotify account access for playback, playlists, listening data, and local token storage. Use explicit music-related prompts and review actions before starting auto-DJ, party rooms, or playlist changes.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger mapping is real, but it is tied to the advertised music-control purpose and does not show hidden or unrelated behavior; users should still confirm before playback, queue, party, or auto-DJ actions when intent is ambiguous.
